_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled, double-blind monotherapy study; 12 weeks of treatment (vs 24 weeks in other studies)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, lixisenatide as monotherapy (adjunct to diet and exercise)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean HbA1c treatment difference vs placebo: lixisenatide 2-step -0.52% (95% CI -0.761, -0.285), p<0.0001; lixisenatide 1-step -0.65% (95% CI -0.891, -0.418), p<0.0001

nct_ctgov.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Lixisenatide in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes for Glycemic Control and Safety Evaluation in Monotherapy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: EFC6015 (add-on to sulfonylurea or SU+metformin, placebo-controlled)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled, double-blind study of lixisenatide added to sulfonylurea alone or combined with metformin; 24-week main treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on sulfonylurea alone or with metformin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean HbA1c change: placebo -0.23%, lixisenatide -0.91%; treatment difference vs placebo -0.69% (95% CI -0.811, -0.560), p<0.0001

nct_ctgov.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Lixisenatide in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes for Glycemic Control and Safety Evaluation, on Top of Sulfonylurea

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhea, dizziness, and hypoglycemia. Rates vs placebo: nausea 25% vs 6%, vomiting 10% vs 2%, headache 9% vs 6%, diarrhea 8% vs 6%, dizziness 7% vs 4%. Serious risks include anaphylaxis/serious hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, hypoglycemia with concomitant sulfonylurea/basal insulin, and renal failure.
target_moa: Lixisenatide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist; it increases glucose-dependent insulin release, decreases glucagon secretion, and slows gastric emptying

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee of 15 voting members convened May 25, 2016; the committee was NOT asked to vote on approval of lixisenatide, only to discuss efficacy/safety and whether issues precluded approval. Most members opined the data demonstrated efficacy and concerns did not preclude approval.

description.text: Submitted final pediatric study report (PK/PD in type 2 diabetes patients ages 10-17) fulfilling a postmarketing requirement; no new indication added

citations.quote: 3102-1 Conduct a repeat dose, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) study evaluating Adlyxin (lixisenatide) in patients with type 2 diabetes ages 10 to 17 years (inclusive) that are insufficiently controlled with metformin and/or basal insulin. Subjects will be randomized to lixisenatide or placebo. Titration will occur every 2 weeks increasing the dose from 5 mcg to 10 mcg then to 20 mcg.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under standard (not priority) review.

summary.text: Adlyxin (lixisenatide) was reviewed as a standard NDA (208471, received July 27, 2015) and approved based on efficacy from nine placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials with an integrated safety database of twenty Phase 2/3 studies including the ELIXA cardiovascular outcome study. A prior NDA (204961) had been withdrawn by the applicant in 2013; the present application was approved on the first review cycle after an Advisory Committee meeting on May 25, 2016.

citations.quote: Based on my review of the clinical data, there is evidence of effectiveness from nine placebo-controlled phase 3 trials. The safety profile is acceptable, based on review of an integrated safety database of twenty phase 2/3 studies, including the cardiovascular outcome study (ELIXA).
An NDA for lixisenatide (NDA204961) was originally submitted on December 20, 2012 but was subsequently withdrawn on September 10, 2013.

requirement.text: 3102-1: Conduct a repeat-dose PK/PD study evaluating Adlyxin in type 2 diabetes patients ages 10 to 17 years insufficiently controlled with metformin and/or basal insulin (randomized to lixisenatide or placebo).

citations.quote: 3102-1 Conduct a repeat dose, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) study evaluating Adlyxin (lixisenatide) in patients with type 2 diabetes ages 10 to 17 years (inclusive) that are insufficiently controlled with metformin and/or basal insulin. Subjects will be randomized to lixisenatide or placebo. Titration will occur every 2 weeks increasing the dose from 5 mcg to 10 mcg then to 20 mcg.

requirement.text: 3102-2: Conduct a 24-week randomized controlled efficacy and safety study comparing Adlyxin with placebo in type 2 diabetes patients ages 10 to 17 years, followed by a 28-week double-blind controlled extension, on background metformin and/or basal insulin.

citations.quote: 3102-2 Conduct a 24-week, randomized, controlled efficacy and safety study comparing Adlyxin (lixisenatide) with placebo in patients with type 2 diabetes ages 10 to 17 years (inclusive), followed by a 28-week double-blind controlled extension. Subjects will be on a background of metformin and/or basal insulin at a stable dose. This trial should not be initiated until the results of the pediatric PK/PD study (PMR 3102-1) have been submitted to and reviewed by the Agency.

requirement.text: 3102-3: Perform immunogenicity testing on anti-drug antibody (ADA)-positive samples from clinical studies to determine the incidence of neutralizing antibodies and anti-lixisenatide antibodies cross-reactive with endogenous GLP-1 and glucagon.

citations.quote: 3102-3 Perform immunogenicity testing on anti-drug antibody (ADA)-positive samples from clinical studies of type 2 diabetes patients treated with lixisenatide to determine the incidence of neutralizing antibodies (NAb) and anti-lixisenatide antibodies that are cross-reactive with endogenous GLP-1 and glucagon peptides and are capable of neutralizing these endogenous peptides.
